title: Soufflé au Fromage
shortDescription: Classic French cheese soufflé with Gruyère
note: Serve immediately; soufflés deflate quickly after baking.
introCopy: This ethereal cheese soufflé is a cornerstone of French bistro cooking. The key is a well-made béchamel base, stiffly beaten egg whites, and confidence—don't open the oven door during baking.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Generously butter a 1.5-litre soufflé dish and dust with grated Parmesan or breadcrumbs.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute to form a roux. Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth. Cook, stirring, until thick, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Gruyère, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until cheese melts. Beat in egg yolks one at a time.
In a clean bowl, whisk egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold a spoonful into the cheese base to lighten, then gently fold in remaining whites.
Pour into prepared dish. Run your thumb around the rim to create a 'top hat' effect. Bake for 20-25 minutes until risen and golden. Serve immediately.

title: Steak au Poivre
shortDescription: Peppercorn-crusted steak with cognac cream sauce
note: Use a heavy-bottomed pan for the best crust.
introCopy: This luxurious Parisian bistro classic pairs a perfectly seared steak with a rich, creamy cognac and peppercorn sauce. It's indulgent, impressive, and ready in minutes.

steps.text: Pat steaks dry. Press crushed peppercorns into both sides of each steak, then season with salt.
Heat oil and 1 tbsp butter in a heavy pan over high heat. Sear steaks for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Remove and rest.
Reduce heat to medium. Add cognac to the pan (be careful—it may flame). Scrape up browned bits, then add stock and simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in cream and any resting juices. Simmer until thickened. Swirl in remaining butter. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Plate steaks, spoon sauce over, and serve immediately with frites or mash.

title: Salade Lyonnaise
shortDescription: Frisée salad with bacon, croutons, and poached egg
note: The runny yolk acts as additional dressing.
introCopy: From Lyon, the gastronomic capital of France, this composed salad combines bitter frisée, crisp bacon lardons, crunchy croutons, and a perfectly poached egg with a warm vinaigrette.

steps.text: Cook bacon in a pan until crisp. Remove and set aside. In the bacon fat, fry bread cubes until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer with 1 tbsp white wine vinegar. Poach eggs for 3-4 minutes until whites are set but yolks runny. Remove with a slotted spoon.
In a small bowl, whisk together red wine vinegar, mustard, and shallot. Slowly whisk in olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Toss frisée with half the dressing. Divide between plates. Top with bacon, croutons, and a poached egg.
Drizzle remaining dressing over. Serve immediately, encouraging diners to break the yolk into the salad.

title: Crème Brûlée
shortDescription: Silky vanilla custard with caramelized sugar crust
note: Use a kitchen torch for the best caramelization.
introCopy: This iconic French dessert features a rich, creamy vanilla custard beneath a brittle, caramelized sugar shell. The contrast between the silky custard and the crackling topping is pure magic.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F). Heat cream with vanilla pod and seeds until just simmering. Remove from heat and let infuse for 10 minutes.
Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale. Remove vanilla pod from cream, then gradually whisk cream into yolk mixture.
Strain mixture through a fine sieve. Divide between 6 ramekins. Place in a deep roasting tin and pour hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until set but still slightly wobbly in the center. Remove and cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Just before serving, sprinkle 1 tsp sugar evenly over each custard. Caramelize with a blowtorch until golden and bubbling. Let set for 1 minute before serving.

title: Moules Frites
shortDescription: Steamed mussels in white wine with crispy fries
note: Discard any mussels that don't open after cooking.
introCopy: A beloved Belgian-French brasserie dish, moules frites pairs plump mussels steamed in white wine, shallots, and herbs with crispy golden fries for dipping in the fragrant broth.

steps.text: Scrub mussels under cold water. Remove beards and discard any that are open and don't close when tapped.
In a large pot with a lid, melt butter over medium heat. Add shallots and garlic, cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add wine and bring to a boil. Add mussels, cover tightly, and steam for 4-5 minutes, shaking the pot occasionally, until mussels open.
Discard any unopened mussels. Stir in parsley and pepper. Divide mussels and broth between bowls.
Serve immediately with hot fries and baguette for soaking up the broth.

title: Madeleines
shortDescription: Classic French shell-shaped sponge cakes
note: Chilling the batter creates the signature hump.
introCopy: These delicate, buttery little cakes from Commercy in Lorraine are famous for their distinctive shell shape and tender crumb. Proust made them legendary in literature.

ingredients.prepNote: melted and cooled, plus extra for pan

steps.text: Whisk eggs and sugar until pale and thick, about 3-4 minutes. Sift in flour and baking powder, fold gently.
Fold in melted butter, vanilla, and lemon zest until just combined. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Generously butter and flour a madeleine tin.
Spoon batter into molds, filling each about 3/4 full. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden with a signature hump.
Turn out immediately onto a wire rack. Dust with icing sugar if desired. Best served warm or same day.

title: Pissaladière
shortDescription: Provençal onion tart with anchovies and olives
note: The onions should be soft and jammy, not browned.
introCopy: This savory tart from Nice is topped with sweet caramelized onions, briny anchovies, and black olives on a tender, pizza-like crust. It's perfect for lunch or as an apéritif.

steps.text: Make dough: combine flour, salt, and yeast. Add water and oil, mix to a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes. Cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, heat 4 tbsp olive oil in a large pan. Add onions, garlic, and thyme. Cook gently for 40-45 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and golden. Season and cool.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Roll dough into a rectangle and place on an oiled baking sheet. Prick all over with a fork.
Spread onion mixture evenly over dough. Arrange anchovies in a lattice pattern, placing an olive in each diamond.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until crust is golden. Cool slightly, slice, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Éclair au Chocolat
shortDescription: Chocolate-glazed choux pastry with vanilla cream
note: Don't open the oven door while baking choux pastry.
introCopy: These elegant French pastries feature light, airy choux filled with luscious vanilla crème pâtissière and topped with glossy chocolate icing. They're a Parisian pâtisserie staple.

steps.text: Make choux: heat water, butter, and salt to a rolling boil. Remove from heat, add flour all at once, beat vigorously. Return to heat and stir for 1 minute. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in eggs gradually until glossy.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Pipe 12 x 10cm logs onto lined baking sheets. Bake 25-30 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
Make crème pâtissière: heat milk with vanilla pod. Whisk yolks, sugar, and cornflour. Pour in hot milk, whisk, then return to pan. Cook, stirring, until thick. Strain, cover with cling film, cool.
Make glaze: melt chocolate and butter together until smooth. Let cool slightly.
Pierce éclair bottoms, pipe in crème pâtissière. Dip tops in chocolate glaze. Refrigerate until set, at least 30 minutes. Serve chilled.

title: Tarte aux Poireaux
shortDescription: Creamy leek tart with Gruyère and bacon
note: Blind-bake the pastry to prevent a soggy bottom.
introCopy: This elegant savory tart showcases the sweet, delicate flavor of leeks in a creamy custard with Gruyère and bacon. It's a French bistro classic, perfect for lunch with a green salad.

ingredients.prepNote: white and light green parts, sliced

steps.text: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Line a 23cm tart tin with pastry, prick base, and blind-bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans/paper, bake 5 more minutes.
Cook bacon until crisp, remove. In the same pan, melt butter and gently cook leeks for 10-12 minutes until very soft but not colored. Season.
Whisk together eggs, cream, Gruyère, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Spread leeks and bacon in pastry case. Pour over egg mixture. Bake for 30-35 minutes until set and golden.
Cool for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Macaron Framboise
shortDescription: Raspberry-filled French almond meringue cookies
note: Age egg whites for 24 hours for best results.
introCopy: These iconic Parisian treats feature crisp almond meringue shells with ruffled 'feet' and a tender interior, sandwiched with vibrant raspberry buttercream or ganache.

steps.text: Sift ground almonds and icing sugar together twice. Set aside.
Whisk egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add caster sugar, whisking to stiff, glossy peaks. Add food coloring if using.

Fold almond mixture into meringue in three additions using a gentle macaronage technique until mixture flows like lava. Pipe 3cm circles onto lined baking sheets. Tap firmly to release air bubbles. Rest 30-60 minutes until a skin forms.
Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F). Bake for 12-14 minutes. Cool completely on sheets.

Make filling: beat butter, icing sugar, raspberry purée, and lemon juice until fluffy. Pipe onto half the shells, sandwich with remaining shells. Refrigerate 24 hours to mature. Serve at room temperature.

title: Terrine de Campagne
shortDescription: Rustic French country pâté with pork and liver
note: Age for 2-3 days before serving for best flavor.
introCopy: This rustic pâté is a French charcuterie staple, rich with pork, liver, brandy, and aromatics. Serve sliced with cornichons, mustard, and crusty bread.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a terrine mold or loaf tin with overlapping bacon rashers, leaving overhang.
Combine pork, liver, minced bacon, shallots, garlic, eggs, brandy, thyme, allspice, salt, and pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Pack mixture into terrine, press out air pockets. Top with bay leaves. Fold bacon overhang over top. Cover tightly with foil.
Place terrine in a deep roasting tin. Pour hot water halfway up the sides. Bake for 1.5 hours until internal temperature reaches 70°C.
Remove from water bath, cool to room temperature. Weight down with cans or a brick, refrigerate for 2-3 days. Slice and serve with cornichons, mustard, and baguette.

title: Gougères
shortDescription: Savory cheese puffs made with choux pastry
note: Serve warm straight from the oven for best texture.
introCopy: These airy, golden cheese puffs from Burgundy are made with choux pastry and Gruyère. They're a classic French apéritif, perfect with champagne or wine.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Bring water, milk, butter, and salt to a rolling boil. Remove from heat, add flour all at once, beat vigorously until smooth. Return to heat and stir for 1 minute.
Cool for 5 minutes. Beat in eggs one at a time until glossy and smooth. Stir in 120g Gruyère, pepper, and nutmeg.
Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto baking sheets, spacing well. Top each with a pinch of remaining cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until puffed, golden, and crisp. Serve warm.

title: Rillettes de Porc
shortDescription: Slow-cooked shredded pork spread from Tours
note: The fat layer on top preserves the rillettes.
introCopy: This rustic pork spread from the Loire Valley is made by slow-cooking pork in fat until tender, then shredding and potting it. Serve on crusty bread with cornichons.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 140°C (285°F). Place pork, lard, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, allspice, cloves, salt, and pepper in a heavy casserole.
Cover tightly and cook for 4 hours, stirring occasionally, until pork is meltingly tender and falling apart.
Remove herbs and bay leaves. Using two forks, shred the meat finely. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Pack into sterilized jars or a terrine, pressing out air pockets. Pour a layer of melted fat over the top to seal. Cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate for at least 2 days to mature. Serve at room temperature with baguette and cornichons. Keeps for 2 weeks.

title: Kouign-Amann
shortDescription: Caramelized Breton butter cake with flaky layers
note: Best eaten warm on the day of baking.
introCopy: This legendary Breton pastry from Douarnenez features layers of buttery, laminated dough caramelized with sugar. The result is crispy, sticky, and utterly irresistible.

steps.text: Make dough: combine flour, salt, and yeast. Add water and mix to a soft dough. Knead briefly, then rest for 30 minutes.
Roll dough into a 30cm square. Flatten butter between parchment to a 15cm square. Place butter in center of dough, fold corners over to enclose. Roll into a 20x40cm rectangle.
Sprinkle with 50g sugar. Fold into thirds like a letter. Turn 90°, roll out again. Repeat sugar, fold, turn, roll process twice more. Chill 30 minutes if needed.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Butter a 20cm round cake tin and sprinkle with 50g sugar. Roll dough to fit tin, press in, sprinkle remaining sugar on top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until deeply caramelized and golden. Cool 5 minutes, invert onto a plate (caramel side up). Serve warm, torn into pieces.

title: Vichyssoise
shortDescription: Chilled leek and potato soup with cream
note: Serve ice-cold in chilled bowls.
introCopy: This elegant chilled soup, despite its French name, was created in New York but celebrates French technique. Silky-smooth leeks and potatoes are enriched with cream and served cold.

ingredients.prepNote: white and light green parts, sliced

steps.text: Melt butter in a large pot. Add leeks and cook gently for 10 minutes until very soft but not colored.
Add potatoes and stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Blend soup until completely smooth using an immersion or jug blender. Strain through a fine sieve for extra silkiness.
Stir in cream. Season with salt and white pepper. Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Serve ice-cold in chilled bowls, garnished with chives.

title: Gratin Savoyard
shortDescription: Alpine potato gratin with Beaufort cheese and stock
note: Unlike Dauphinois, this uses stock instead of cream.
introCopy: From the Savoie region in the French Alps, this gratin layers thinly sliced potatoes with nutty Beaufort cheese and rich stock. It's hearty, comforting, and perfect après-ski.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Rub a gratin dish generously with the cut garlic, then butter the dish.
Layer half the potatoes in the dish, season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Scatter over half the cheese. Repeat with remaining potatoes and cheese.
Pour over hot stock until it almost reaches the top layer. Dot with butter.
Bake for 60-75 minutes until potatoes are tender and the top is golden and bubbling. Test with a knife.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Profiteroles
shortDescription: Choux buns filled with ice cream and chocolate sauce
note: Assemble just before serving to keep buns crisp.
introCopy: These delightful French dessert puffs are filled with vanilla ice cream and drizzled with warm chocolate sauce. They're elegant, playful, and surprisingly easy.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Make choux: bring water, butter, salt, and sugar to a rolling boil. Remove from heat, add flour all at once, beat until smooth. Return to heat, stir for 1 minute. Cool 5 minutes.
Beat in eggs gradually until glossy. Pipe or spoon 18 walnut-sized mounds onto lined baking sheets.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until puffed, golden, and crisp. Pierce each to release steam. Cool completely.
Make chocolate sauce: heat cream until just simmering. Pour over chocolate, let sit 1 minute, then stir until smooth.
To serve: slice buns in half, fill with a scoop of ice cream, replace tops. Stack 3 per person, drizzle generously with warm chocolate sauce. Serve immediately.

title: Lapin à la Moutarde
shortDescription: Rabbit braised in Dijon mustard cream sauce
note: Chicken can substitute if rabbit is unavailable.
introCopy: This classic French dish from Burgundy features tender rabbit pieces braised with white wine, Dijon mustard, and cream. It's rich, tangy, and deeply satisfying.

steps.text: Pat rabbit dry, season with salt and pepper, then coat each piece with mustard.
Heat oil and butter in a large casserole. Brown rabbit pieces on all sides, about 8 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add shallots and garlic to the pan, cook for 2 minutes. Add wine and stock, bring to a boil, scraping up browned bits.
Return rabbit to the pan with tarragon. Cover and simmer gently for 45-50 minutes until rabbit is tender.
Remove rabbit to a serving dish. Stir cream into sauce, simmer until thickened. Taste and adjust seasoning. Pour over rabbit and serve with potatoes or pasta.

title: Financiers
shortDescription: Almond and brown butter mini cakes
note: Brown butter (beurre noisette) is the flavor secret.
introCopy: These elegant little French cakes, traditionally baked in rectangular molds, are made with ground almonds and brown butter. They're moist, nutty, and utterly moreish.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Generously butter a 12-hole financier or mini muffin tin.
Make brown butter: melt butter in a small pan over medium heat. Continue cooking, swirling, until golden brown with a nutty aroma, about 4-5 minutes. Cool slightly.
Whisk egg whites until frothy but not stiff. Sift in icing sugar, ground almonds, flour, and salt. Fold gently. Fold in brown butter and vanilla.
Divide batter between molds, filling each 3/4 full. Bake for 12-15 minutes until golden and springy.
Cool in tin for 2 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Poulet Rôti au Citron
shortDescription: Classic French roast chicken with lemon and herbs
note: Let the chicken rest before carving for juicier meat.
introCopy: A perfect roast chicken is a cornerstone of French home cooking. This version is scented with lemon, garlic, and herbs, with crispy golden skin and tender, juicy meat.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Pat chicken dry inside and out. Season cavity generously with salt and pepper.
Stuff cavity with lemon quarters, garlic halves, thyme, and rosemary. Rub chicken all over with butter, then drizzle with olive oil. Season skin well.
Place chicken breast-side up in a roasting tin. Squeeze the halved lemon over the top.
Roast for 1 hour 15 minutes, basting every 20 minutes, until skin is golden and juices run clear (internal temp 75°C).
Rest for 15 minutes before carving. Serve with pan juices and roasted vegetables or salad.

title: Oeufs en Cocotte
shortDescription: Baked eggs with cream and herbs in ramekins
note: Watch carefully to avoid overcooking the yolks.
introCopy: These delicate baked eggs are a French breakfast or brunch classic. Cooked gently in a water bath with cream and fresh herbs, they're silky, rich, and elegant.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Generously butter 4 ramekins.
Pour 1 tbsp cream into each ramekin. Crack an egg into each. Season with salt and pepper. Top with chives and Gruyère if using.
Place ramekins in a deep baking dish. Pour hot water into the dish to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until whites are just set but yolks are still runny. Check at 10 minutes—they cook quickly.
Carefully remove ramekins from water bath. Serve immediately with toasted baguette for dipping.

title: Crêpes Salées Complètes
shortDescription: Buckwheat galettes with ham, cheese, and egg
note: Buckwheat batter benefits from resting overnight.
introCopy: These savory buckwheat crêpes from Brittany are traditionally filled with ham, Gruyère, and a fried egg. They're rustic, satisfying, and naturally gluten-free.

steps.text: Make batter: whisk buckwheat flour, salt, and egg. Gradually whisk in water until smooth. Stir in melted butter. Rest for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Heat a crêpe pan or non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Brush with butter.
Pour a ladleful of batter into the pan, swirl to coat thinly. Cook for 1-2 minutes until edges lift. Flip and cook 30 seconds.

Place 2 slices ham and a handful of Gruyère in the center. Crack an egg onto the cheese. Season with pepper. Fold edges to form a square, leaving egg visible. Cover and cook until egg white is set but yolk runny, 2-3 minutes.
Slide onto a plate. Repeat with remaining batter and fillings. Serve immediately.

title: Soupe au Pistou
shortDescription: Provençal vegetable soup with basil pistou
note: The pistou (basil paste) is stirred in at the end.
introCopy: This vibrant vegetable soup from Provence is loaded with summer beans, courgettes, and tomatoes, then finished with a punchy basil and garlic pistou similar to pesto.

steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot. Add onion and carrots, cook gently for 5 minutes. Add courgettes and green beans, cook 5 more minutes.
Add tomatoes, white beans, and stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Add pasta and cook until tender, about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, make pistou: pound basil, garlic, and a pinch of salt in a mortar and pestle (or use a food processor). Stir in Parmesan, then gradually add olive oil until you have a thick paste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Stir a generous spoonful of pistou into each bowl at the table.

title: Pan Bagnat
shortDescription: Provençal tuna and vegetable sandwich from Nice
note: Press the sandwich for at least 30 minutes before serving.
introCopy: This iconic Niçoise sandwich is essentially a salade niçoise stuffed into a crusty roll, then pressed and weighted so the olive oil-dressed ingredients meld together beautifully. Perfect for picnics.

steps.text: Rub the cut sides of the rolls with the garlic halves. Drizzle the bottom halves generously with olive oil and vinegar.
Layer on the tuna, tomatoes, eggs, onion, pepper, anchovies (if using), olives, and basil. Season each layer with salt and pepper.
Drizzle the remaining olive oil over the top. Replace the top halves of the rolls and press down firmly.
Wrap each sandwich tightly in parchment or foil. Weight down with a heavy pan or cans and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, ideally 2-3 hours.
Unwrap and cut into wedges to serve.

title: Canelés Bordelais
shortDescription: Caramelized custard cakes from Bordeaux
note: Traditional copper molds produce the best crust.
introCopy: These stunning little cakes from Bordeaux have a dark, caramelized exterior and a soft, custardy center flavored with rum and vanilla. They require special fluted molds but are worth the effort.

steps.text: Heat milk, butter, and vanilla pod with seeds until butter melts. Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature. Remove vanilla pod.
Whisk eggs, yolk, and sugar until pale. Sift in flour and whisk until smooth. Gradually whisk in the cooled milk mixture and rum. Strain through a fine sieve.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 24 hours, ideally 48 hours. This rest is essential for texture.
Preheat oven to 250°C (480°F). Generously butter canelé molds. Pour batter into molds, filling 3/4 full.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce heat to 180°C (350°F) and bake for 45-50 minutes more until very dark brown and caramelized. Turn out immediately onto a wire rack. Best eaten the same day.
